task_instance: Draft a blog post announcing 'QuickSync', a new AI-powered meeting scheduling feature for a B2B SaaS product, targeted at marketing operations managers, with 4 key messages, conversational/professional tone (no brand voice file configured), ~650 words, following the skill's Blog Post content spec (headline options, hook intro, organized sections with subheadings, CTA, SEO recommendations, brand voice note, and next-step suggestions).
evidence: Created brief.txt (sample user input: content type, topic, audience, key messages, tone, length) and draft-content.md (the deliverable) in the work directory using only the Write tool -- no shell/code execution was needed since the deliverable is pure text. Read draft-content.md back to verify: it contains 3 headline options, a hook-driven introduction, 4 subheaded body sections each covering one of the 4 key messages, a closing CTA section, an SEO recommendations block (primary keyword, keyword placement, meta title/description, internal/external linking, image alt text), a brand-voice note (explicitly following the skill's instruction to ask about brand voice and default to a neutral professional tone since none was configured), and a suggested-next-steps list plus the skill's closing question about revisions/channel variations. Word count of the post body is ~640 words, matching the requested ~650-word target. All of the skill's required Blog Post elements (Content Generation by Type > Blog Post, SEO Considerations, Output sections) are present and verified by direct inspection of the file content -- no code execution, binary output, or external/connector tools were required at any point.
